newsitem.title: UK: U.S. wants more info on GrandMet, Guinness.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wants more info on GrandMet, Guinness.

text.p: Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc said on Friday they had received a second request from U.S. competition authorities for information on their planned 23.8 billion pound ($39.2 billion) merger.
Analysts had expected U.S. authorities to take a close look at the merger, which has been opposed by French luxury goods firm LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, a major shareholder in both firms.
GrandMet and Guinness said the European Union's competition commission had until 2200 GMT on Friday to decide whether it would conduct a second-stage probe into the merger.
The companies said they would make a further announcement in due course.
GrandMet's shares slipped 1.0 pence to 602.5 by 0945 GMT, while Guinness fell 2.5 pence to 602.5.
The companies' merger would create a global food and drinks giant combining brands like Guinness' world-famous stout with GrandMet's Burger King restaurant chain.
LVMH has fought the deal since it was unveiled in May, raising its stake in GrandMet on Thursday to over six percent as part of its attack to foil the merger.

The French firm, which holds about 14 percent of Guinness' shares, wants to create a group combining its Moet & Chandon and Hennessy brands with Guinness' Johnny Walker, Dewars and Gordon's Gin labels.
But Guinness and GrandMet have defended the merger by arguing their brands are highly complementary and would create shareholder value.
